body:
Rachel Kim: want to tighten up our reference-call prep. seeing the same prospect questions over and over (SLA, fallbacks, cost). can we drop a shared question bank here + any “avoid” notes? goal is we send the ref customer a 1-pager w/ what to expect + we’re not scrambling 10 min before.

Miguel Santos: +1. cascade and atlas both asked for an agenda ahead of time. customers are happier when we tell them what NOT to answer too.

Markus Klein: from SE side, the top 3 technical buckets i hear on late-stage calls:
1) “what’s the SLA actually cover? uptime vs latency?”
2) “what happens when capacity is constrained / region issues? do you have fallback?”
3) “how do we control $/1M tokens (batching/caching/quant) without wrecking latency?”

Simran Kaur: adding: “how do rollouts/version pinning work?” and “how do you measure + debug latency (token breakdown)?” those come up a lot when prospects compare us to DIY.

Tyler Benson: if we’re making a standard question bank, can we also include a section that says: please don’t share contract pricing, specific GPU counts, or other customer names. (legal got twitchy last time)

Camila Reyes: yes please. we can package this into the reference-call brief template. for now, dump questions + suggested framing here, and i’ll have Ethan fold it into the doc.

Avery Johnson: AE POV: the prospect almost always asks the reference customer:
- “did Redwood actually hit the numbers they promised?”
- “how painful was onboarding + migration?”
- “did support show up when things broke?”
…and then they ask me the commercial stuff separately.

Isabelle Laurent: reminder: please log the call outcome in HubSpot after (deal assoc + “reference call used” checkbox). otherwise we can’t prove influence. :pray:

Rachel Kim: ok starting a question bank draft below. pls reply with edits/additions. (we can later move to Drive + link it in Confluence)

Rachel Kim: 
QUESTION BANK (prospects ask references)

A) Reliability / SLA
- Q: What SLA are you on and has Redwood met it?
  - Suggested answer: focus on experience (uptime/incident comms), avoid quoting exact contract terms. If asked, redirect to AE/Redwood team for specifics.
- Q: What latency do you see in prod (p50/p95)?
  - Suggested answer: share relative improvements and context (traffic pattern, prompt lengths). Use ranges if needed.
- Q: How does incident response work?
  - Suggested answer: “we had a clear escalation path, quick acknowledgment, and regular updates.” Avoid naming individual engineers.

B) Fallbacks / capacity / graceful degradation
- Q: What happens if your preferred model/region is saturated?
- Q: Do you use automatic fallback to model variants or other regions?
- Q: Have you actually experienced fallback? did quality change?
  - Suggested answer: describe the policy at a high level (e.g., canary + fallback, compatible variants). Don’t share internal routing config values.

C) Cost / unit economics
- Q: How do you keep spend predictable? what levers did you use?
- Q: Did batching/caching help? any gotchas?
- Q: How do you attribute token cost per feature/team?
  - Suggested answer: talk about Console breakdowns and operational controls. Avoid sharing exact $ unless explicitly approved.

D) Deployment + security (common esp for Private/VPC)
- Q: Why Dedicated/Private vs hosted API?
- Q: Any security/compliance hurdles (KMS, audit logs, data residency)?
- Q: What did legal/security review focus on?
  - Suggested answer: stick to what’s public/approved; mention “customer-managed networking”/“audit logs available” at a high level.

E) Implementation / migration
- Q: How long from kickoff to production?
- Q: What was hardest part of integration?
- Q: Did you need to change prompts/evals?
- Q: How does version pinning / rollouts work for you?

F) Product quality + roadmap trust
- Q: Any regressions? how do you catch them?
- Q: Do you feel Redwood is stable + improving?

G) Support + partnership
- Q: How responsive is CS/SE? do you get proactive guidance?
- Q: If you could redo anything, what would you do differently?

AVOID LIST (for reference customers)
- Please don’t share: pricing/discounts, contract terms, other vendor names unless already public, specific GPU counts/architectures, sensitive security details, or anything covered by NDA.

PREP NOTES (for Redwood internal)
- Send agenda + 5–8 likely questions to reference customer 48h prior.
- Confirm if metrics can be exact vs ranges.
- Make sure AE owns commercial questions.

Miguel Santos: love this. add one more i hear constantly: “did you consider building/hosting vLLM/TGI yourself? why didn’t you?” refs usually answer well if we frame it as focus + operational burden.

Markus Klein: +1. add under Implementation:
- Q: Why not self-host?
  - Suggested answer: “we didn’t want to staff a 24/7 inference platform team; Redwood gave predictable perf + operations out of the box.”

Simran Kaur: small tweak on fallbacks: prospects ask about “what triggers fallback?” and “can you pin to no-fallback for quality-sensitive routes?” might be good to include:
- Q: Can you control fallback behavior per route/use case?

Avery Johnson: + add “data retention / training” question. prospects love asking the reference customer “did you have concerns about your data being used to train models?”

Rachel Kim: good call. i’ll add:
- Q: Does Redwood use your data for training? how do you handle retention?
  - Suggested answer: “we got clear answers from Redwood on data handling; specifics from Redwood security/legal.”

Tyler Benson: process note: can we standardize that *CS* sends the prep doc, not AE? reduces randomness + keeps tone consistent.

Camila Reyes: yes. CS sends, AE + SE review. we’ll put that in the intake/approval process doc.

Isabelle Laurent: for tracking, can we add a line in PREP NOTES: “create meeting in calendar w/ deal ID in title” or at least note the deal link in the Slack thread? makes reporting 10x easier.

Miguel Santos: also: please set expectations w/ the ref customer on duration (20–30 min) and the “cooldown” (max X calls/month). customers ask that up front.

Rachel Kim: adding:
- Set call length: 25 min default, hard stop at 30.
- Set load: default max 2 calls/month per ref customer unless customer opts in.

Markus Klein: one more technical Q that pops up late-stage Dedicated:
- “how do you guarantee capacity at peak? any burst?”
refs can answer as “we reserved capacity; Redwood handled scaling policies w/ us.” keep it high-level.

Simran Kaur: and “how do you monitor quality drift?” refs like to mention prompt sets/evals if they used them.

Avery Johnson: :thumbsup: can someone put this into the actual brief template link? i keep grabbing old versions.

Camila Reyes: Ethan is updating the template this week. for now, i’ll paste a temp doc link in #marketing once it’s in Drive. we’ll also post in #announcements when the new process is live.

Rachel Kim: thanks all. i’ll clean up + send to Ethan/Tyler to incorporate. if you hear new questions in calls this week, reply here so we keep it current.
